title: Reporting chain depth
context: How many levels below the CEO is each employee?
task: Return name and depth (0 for the employee with no manager, 1 for their reports, etc.) using a recursive CTE.
hint: Anchor: manager_id IS NULL, depth 0; recurse via manager_id.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE chain(employee_id, name, depth) AS (SELECT employee_id, name, 0 FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.employee_id, e.name, c.depth + 1 FROM employees e JOIN chain c ON c.employee_id = e.manager_id) SELECT name, depth FROM chain;

title: Everyone under a VP
context: All employees (direct or indirect) reporting to 'VP Ads'.
task: Return name for all employees below the employee named 'VP Ads', at any depth.
hint: Anchor on the VP's employee_id, recurse downward, exclude the VP.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE sub(employee_id) AS (SELECT employee_id FROM employees WHERE name = 'VP Ads' UNION ALL SELECT e.employee_id FROM employees e JOIN sub s ON s.employee_id = e.manager_id) SELECT e.name FROM employees e JOIN sub s ON s.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.name <> 'VP Ads';

title: Total payroll under each L7
context: Roll up salaries through the hierarchy.
task: Return name (of each L7) and org_payroll = sum of salaries of everyone below them (excluding themselves).
hint: Recursive CTE carrying the root id, then GROUP BY root.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE t(root_id, employee_id) AS (SELECT employee_id, employee_id FROM employees WHERE level = 'L7' UNION ALL SELECT t.root_id, e.employee_id FROM employees e JOIN t ON t.employee_id = e.manager_id) SELECT r.name, SUM(e.salary) AS org_payroll FROM t JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = t.employee_id JOIN employees r ON r.employee_id = t.root_id WHERE t.employee_id <> t.root_id GROUP BY t.root_id;

title: Management path as text
context: Breadcrumb like 'Sundar P > VP Search > Search Mgr 1 > Search Eng 1-2'.
task: Return name and path (names joined by ' > ' from the top) for employees at level 'L3'.
hint: Carry a text path in the recursive CTE.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE p(employee_id, name, level, path) AS (SELECT employee_id, name, level, name FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.employee_id, e.name, e.level, p.path || ' > ' || e.name FROM employees e JOIN p ON p.employee_id = e.manager_id) SELECT name, path FROM p WHERE level = 'L3';

title: Search sessions (30-minute gap)
context: Sessionise searches: a new session starts when the gap from the previous search by the same user exceeds 30 minutes or the day changes.
task: Return user_id and sessions = number of sessions.
hint: LAG over (date, time); minutes = hh*60+mm; count boundaries.
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT user_id, search_date, CAST(SUBSTR(search_time,1,2) AS INTEGER) * 60 + CAST(SUBSTR(search_time,4,2) AS INTEGER) AS m, LAG(search_date) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY search_date, search_time) AS pd, LAG(CAST(SUBSTR(search_time,1,2) AS INTEGER) * 60 + CAST(SUBSTR(search_time,4,2) AS INTEGER)) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY search_date, search_time) AS pm FROM searches) SELECT user_id, SUM(CASE WHEN pd IS NULL OR pd <> search_date OR m - pm > 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sessions FROM s GROUP BY user_id;

title: Refined queries
context: A refinement = the next search by the same user on the same day whose query starts with the previous query and is longer.
task: Return user_id, query (as original) and next_query for such pairs.
hint: LEAD(query) and compare with LIKE query || '%'.
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT user_id, search_date, query, LEAD(query) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, search_date ORDER BY search_time) AS next_query FROM searches) SELECT user_id, query AS original, next_query FROM s WHERE next_query IS NOT NULL AND next_query LIKE query || ' %';

title: Did refining help?
context: Compare click rate of refined queries vs originals in refinement pairs.
task: Return original_ctr_pct and refined_ctr_pct (1 dp) across all refinement pairs.
hint: Pair via LEAD, then aggregate clicked and next clicked.
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT user_id, search_date, query, clicked, LEAD(query) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, search_date ORDER BY search_time) AS nq, LEAD(clicked) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, search_date ORDER BY search_time) AS nc FROM searches) SELECT ROUND(AVG(clicked) * 100, 1) AS original_ctr_pct, ROUND(AVG(nc) * 100, 1) AS refined_ctr_pct FROM s WHERE nq IS NOT NULL AND nq LIKE query || ' %';

title: Advertiser rank by ROAS within category
context: Category leaderboards.
task: Return category, advertiser, roas (2 dp) and rk = RANK() by roas descending within category, for campaigns with cost > 0.
hint: Aggregate then RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ...).
answer: WITH r AS (SELECT c.category, c.advertiser, SUM(i.revenue) / SUM(i.cost) AS roas FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id HAVING SUM(i.cost) > 0) SELECT category, advertiser, ROUND(roas, 2) AS roas, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY roas DESC) AS rk FROM r;

title: Cumulative spend vs budget
context: Day-by-day pacing for campaign 1.
task: Return impression_date, daily_spend (2 dp) and cumulative_spend (2 dp) for campaign_id = 1, ordered by date.
hint: SUM() OVER (ORDER BY date).
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT impression_date, SUM(cost) AS daily_spend FROM ad_impressions WHERE campaign_id = 1 GROUP BY impression_date) SELECT impression_date, ROUND(daily_spend, 2) AS daily_spend, ROUND(SUM(daily_spend) OVER (ORDER BY impression_date), 2) AS cumulative_spend FROM d;

title: Campaigns ahead of pace
context: Spend share > time-elapsed share, as of 2025-07-31.
task: Return advertiser, spend_pct (1 dp) = spend/budget*100 and time_pct (1 dp) = elapsed days/total days*100 (capped at 100), where spend_pct > time_pct.
hint: MIN(100, elapsed*100/total) via CASE.
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT campaign_id, SUM(cost) AS spend FROM ad_impressions GROUP BY campaign_id) SELECT c.advertiser, ROUND(s.spend * 100.0 / c.budget, 1) AS spend_pct, ROUND(MIN(100.0, (julianday(MIN(c.end_date, '2025-07-31')) - julianday(c.start_date)) * 100.0 / (julianday(c.end_date) - julianday(c.start_date))), 1) AS time_pct FROM ad_campaigns c JOIN s ON s.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE s.spend * 100.0 / c.budget > MIN(100.0, (julianday(MIN(c.end_date, '2025-07-31')) - julianday(c.start_date)) * 100.0 / (julianday(c.end_date) - julianday(c.start_date)));

title: Week-over-week search growth
context: Weekly volume with % change.
task: Return week (strftime '%Y-%W'), searches and wow_pct (1 dp) = (searches − previous week) / previous week * 100, ordered by week.
hint: LAG in a CTE; guard divide by zero with NULLIF.
answer: WITH w AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%W', search_date) AS week, COUNT(*) AS searches FROM searches GROUP BY week) SELECT week, searches, ROUND((searches - LAG(searches) OVER (ORDER BY week)) * 100.0 / NULLIF(LAG(searches) OVER (ORDER BY week), 0), 1) AS wow_pct FROM w;

title: 7-day rolling CTR
context: Smooth the daily search CTR.
task: Return search_date, ctr_pct (1 dp) and rolling7 (1 dp, average of daily CTR over current and 6 preceding rows), ordered by date.
hint: Daily AVG(clicked) then AVG OVER a frame.
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT search_date, AVG(clicked) * 100 AS ctr FROM searches GROUP BY search_date) SELECT search_date, ROUND(ctr, 1) AS ctr_pct, ROUND(AVG(ctr) OVER (ORDER BY search_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 1) AS rolling7 FROM d;

title: Salary quartiles within org
context: Compensation fairness review.
task: Return org, name, salary and quartile = NTILE(4) over salary descending within org.
hint: NTILE(4) OVER (PARTITION BY org ORDER BY salary DESC).
answer: SELECT org, name, salary, NTILE(4) OVER (PARTITION BY org ORDER BY salary DESC) AS quartile FROM employees;

title: Campaign share of category clicks
context: Concentration per category.
task: Return category, advertiser and pct_of_category (1 dp) = campaign clicks / category clicks * 100.
hint: SUM OVER (PARTITION BY category).
answer: WITH k AS (SELECT c.category, c.advertiser, SUM(i.clicked) AS clicks FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id) SELECT category, advertiser, ROUND(clicks * 100.0 / SUM(clicks) OVER (PARTITION BY category), 1) AS pct_of_category FROM k;

title: Week-1 search activation by signup month
context: Did new users search within 7 days of signing up?
task: Return signup_month (YYYY-MM) and activated_pct (1 dp) = users with a search within 7 days of signup / users in that month * 100.
hint: EXISTS with julianday window inside AVG(CASE).
answer: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', u.signup_date) AS signup_month, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM searches s WHERE s.user_id = u.user_id AND julianday(s.search_date) - julianday(u.signup_date) BETWEEN 0 AND 7) THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) * 100, 1) AS activated_pct FROM users u GROUP BY signup_month;

title: Monthly retained searchers
context: Users who searched in month m and m-1.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM) and retained count, ordered by month, only months with retained > 0.
hint: Distinct (user, month) self-join on previous month.
answer: WITH um AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, strftime('%Y-%m', search_date) AS month FROM searches) SELECT a.month, COUNT(*) AS retained FROM um a JOIN um b ON b.user_id = a.user_id AND b.month = strftime('%Y-%m', date(a.month || '-01', '-1 month')) GROUP BY a.month ORDER BY a.month;

title: Stickiness
context: Average DAU divided by MAU per month.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM), mau (distinct searchers in the month), avg_dau (2 dp) and stickiness_pct (1 dp) = avg_dau / mau * 100.
hint: Daily distinct counts averaged per month, joined to monthly distinct counts.
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', search_date) AS month, search_date, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS dau FROM searches GROUP BY search_date), m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', search_date) AS month, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS mau FROM searches GROUP BY month) SELECT m.month, m.mau, ROUND(AVG(d.dau), 2) AS avg_dau, ROUND(AVG(d.dau) * 100.0 / m.mau, 1) AS stickiness_pct FROM m JOIN d ON d.month = m.month GROUP BY m.month;

title: Longest daily search streak
context: Consecutive days with at least one search, per user.
task: Return user_id and longest_streak.
hint: Distinct dates, ROW_NUMBER, date(d, -rn days) grouping.
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, search_date FROM searches), g AS (SELECT user_id, search_date, date(search_date, '-' || ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY search_date) || ' days') AS grp FROM d), s AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS streak FROM g GROUP BY user_id, grp) SELECT user_id, MAX(streak) AS longest_streak FROM s GROUP BY user_id;

title: Median CPC per campaign
context: Average CPC is skewed by a few pricey clicks.
task: Return advertiser and median_cpc (2 dp) over clicked impressions.
hint: ROW_NUMBER/COUNT partitioned by campaign, clicked = 1 only.
answer: WITH c AS (SELECT i.campaign_id, i.cost, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.campaign_id ORDER BY i.cost) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY i.campaign_id) AS cnt FROM ad_impressions i WHERE i.clicked = 1) SELECT a.advertiser, ROUND(AVG(c.cost), 2) AS median_cpc FROM c JOIN ad_campaigns a ON a.campaign_id = c.campaign_id WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2) GROUP BY c.campaign_id;

title: Top-decile salaries
context: Who is in the top 10% of pay?
task: Return name and salary where PERCENT_RANK over salary ascending >= 0.9.
hint: PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary).
answer: SELECT name, salary FROM (SELECT name, salary, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS pr FROM employees) WHERE pr >= 0.9;

title: Position-1 lift
context: How much better is position 1 than the rest, per campaign?
task: Return advertiser, p1_ctr (1 dp) and other_ctr (1 dp) and lift (2 dp) = p1_ctr / other_ctr, for campaigns with impressions in both groups and other_ctr > 0.
hint: Conditional AVG for each group; NULLIF to guard.
answer: WITH t AS (SELECT c.advertiser, AVG(CASE WHEN i.position = 1 THEN i.clicked END) * 100 AS p1, AVG(CASE WHEN i.position > 1 THEN i.clicked END) * 100 AS oth FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id) SELECT advertiser, ROUND(p1, 1) AS p1_ctr, ROUND(oth, 1) AS other_ctr, ROUND(p1 / oth, 2) AS lift FROM t WHERE p1 IS NOT NULL AND oth > 0;

title: Search-then-click within 1 day
context: Impressions clicked by a user who searched the same category the same or previous day.
task: Return campaign_id and assisted_clicks = clicked impressions where the user has a search in the campaign's category with search_date in [impression_date − 1, impression_date].
hint: EXISTS with a date window and category match.
answer: SELECT i.campaign_id, COUNT(*) AS assisted_clicks FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id WHERE i.clicked = 1 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM searches s WHERE s.user_id = i.user_id AND s.category = c.category AND s.search_date BETWEEN date(i.impression_date, '-1 day') AND i.impression_date) GROUP BY i.campaign_id;

title: Searches by category × device
context: Wide table for the intent-by-device report.
task: Return category, mobile, desktop, tablet = search counts per device.
hint: Conditional COUNT after joining users.
answer: SELECT s.category, SUM(CASE WHEN u.device = 'mobile' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS mobile, SUM(CASE WHEN u.device = 'desktop' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS desktop, SUM(CASE WHEN u.device = 'tablet' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS tablet FROM searches s JOIN users u ON u.user_id = s.user_id GROUP BY s.category;

title: Daily impressions including zero days for campaign 3
context: Pacing charts need every day of the flight.
task: Return day and impressions for every date from campaign 3's start_date to end_date (0 where none), ordered by day.
hint: Recursive date series bounded by the campaign's dates.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE days(day) AS (SELECT start_date FROM ad_campaigns WHERE campaign_id = 3 UNION ALL SELECT date(day, '+1 day') FROM days WHERE day < (SELECT end_date FROM ad_campaigns WHERE campaign_id = 3)) SELECT days.day, COUNT(i.impression_id) AS impressions FROM days LEFT JOIN ad_impressions i ON i.impression_date = days.day AND i.campaign_id = 3 GROUP BY days.day ORDER BY days.day;

title: Second-highest salary per org
context: Succession planning.
task: Return org and second_salary (DENSE_RANK = 2 by salary desc within org).
hint: DENSE_RANK per org.
answer: SELECT org, salary AS second_salary FROM (SELECT org, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY org ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rk FROM employees) WHERE rk = 2 GROUP BY org;

title: Managers with too many reports
context: More than 4 direct reports.
task: Return manager name (as manager) and reports for managers with more than 4 direct reports.
hint: GROUP BY manager_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 4, join for the name.
answer: SELECT m.name AS manager, COUNT(*) AS reports FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id = e.manager_id GROUP BY e.manager_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 4;

title: Level pay range by location
context: Same level, different city — how wide is the spread?
task: Return level, location, min_salary, max_salary and spread = max − min, for level/location groups with 2+ employees.
hint: GROUP BY level, location HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2.
answer: SELECT level, location, MIN(salary) AS min_salary, MAX(salary) AS max_salary, MAX(salary) - MIN(salary) AS spread FROM employees GROUP BY level, location HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

title: Searches, impressions and clicks per user without fan-out
context: Three facts per user, one row each, no inflation.
task: Return user_id, searches, impressions, ad_clicks for every user in users (0s where none).
hint: Separate CTEs, LEFT JOIN from users.
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS searches FROM searches GROUP BY user_id), a AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS impressions, SUM(clicked) AS ad_clicks FROM ad_impressions GROUP BY user_id) SELECT u.user_id, COALESCE(s.searches, 0) AS searches, COALESCE(a.impressions, 0) AS impressions, COALESCE(a.ad_clicks, 0) AS ad_clicks FROM users u LEFT JOIN s ON s.user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN a ON a.user_id = u.user_id;

title: Queries making up 50% of searches
context: Head vs tail of search demand.
task: Return query and searches for the most-searched queries whose cumulative share (desc, ties by query) reaches 50% — include the query that crosses 50%.
hint: Running SUM with 1 PRECEDING vs 0.5 × total.
answer: WITH q AS (SELECT query, COUNT(*) AS searches FROM searches GROUP BY query), c AS (SELECT query, searches, SUM(searches) OVER (ORDER BY searches DESC, query ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS prev_cum, SUM(searches) OVER () AS total FROM q) SELECT query, searches FROM c WHERE COALESCE(prev_cum, 0) < 0.5 * total;

title: Users who clicked before converting elsewhere
context: Users with a click on one campaign and a conversion on a different campaign later.
task: Return DISTINCT user_id where a clicked (non-converted) impression on campaign A is followed on a later date by a converted impression on campaign B ≠ A.
hint: Self join ad_impressions on user_id with date and campaign inequality.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT a.user_id FROM ad_impressions a JOIN ad_impressions b ON b.user_id = a.user_id AND b.campaign_id <> a.campaign_id AND b.impression_date > a.impression_date WHERE a.clicked = 1 AND a.converted = 0 AND b.converted = 1;

title: Campaigns whose every click converted
context: Suspiciously perfect (min 3 clicks).
task: Return advertiser and clicks for campaigns with 3+ clicks where every clicked impression converted.
hint: HAVING SUM(clicked) >= 3 AND SUM(clicked) = SUM(converted).
answer: SELECT c.advertiser, SUM(i.clicked) AS clicks FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id HAVING SUM(i.clicked) >= 3 AND SUM(i.clicked) = SUM(i.converted);

title: First query vs most frequent query per user
context: Does the first search predict the habit?
task: Return user_id, first_query and top_query (most searched; ties by query) only where they differ.
hint: FIRST_VALUE for first; ROW_NUMBER on counts for top.
answer: WITH f AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, FIRST_VALUE(query) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY search_date, search_time, search_id) AS first_query FROM searches), c AS (SELECT user_id, query, COUNT(*) AS n FROM searches GROUP BY user_id, query), t AS (SELECT user_id, query AS top_query FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY n DESC, query) AS rn FROM c) WHERE rn = 1) SELECT f.user_id, f.first_query, t.top_query FROM f JOIN t ON t.user_id = f.user_id WHERE f.first_query <> t.top_query;

title: Net value per campaign for the advertiser
context: Advertiser profit = revenue − cost; flag unprofitable campaigns.
task: Return advertiser, revenue (2 dp), cost (2 dp), net (2 dp) and verdict ('profitable' if net > 0 else 'loss').
hint: Aggregates plus CASE on the difference.
answer: SELECT c.advertiser, ROUND(SUM(i.revenue), 2) AS revenue, ROUND(SUM(i.cost), 2) AS cost, ROUND(SUM(i.revenue) - SUM(i.cost), 2) AS net, CASE WHEN SUM(i.revenue) - SUM(i.cost) > 0 THEN 'profitable' ELSE 'loss' END AS verdict FROM ad_impressions i JOIN ad_campaigns c ON c.campaign_id = i.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id;
